entities.summary:
Jordan of Saxony (born c. 1190, died 1237) was the pivotal second Master General of the Dominican Order, whose leadership from 1222 until his death solidified the nascent mendicant movement and propelled its rapid expansion across Europe. A German Catholic priest, he succeeded Saint Dominic de Guzmán and became instrumental in shaping the Order of Preachers into a formidable intellectual and pastoral force in the 13th century. His tenure marked a critical period of growth, institutionalization, and academic development, ensuring the Dominicans' lasting impact on medieval theology, education, and Church reform.

Elected Master General at the second General Chapter in Paris in 1222, Jordan immediately embarked on an ambitious program of recruitment and consolidation. He possessed a remarkable personal charisma, reportedly attracting over 1,000 new members to the order, including such future luminaries as Albertus Magnus, whom he personally received into the Dominicans in Bologna. Jordan significantly expanded the order's presence in universities, particularly in Paris and Bologna, emphasizing rigorous theological study alongside preaching. He authored the *Libellus de principiis Ordinis Praedicatorum* (Booklet on the Beginnings of the Order of Preachers), a foundational historical account and spiritual guide that remains a primary source for the early Dominican charism.
